evals.prompt:
Here's an approved spec:

### Title
Self-service order tracking page

### Why
Customers email support constantly asking where their order is. A self-service view cuts that support load.

### Who
As a logged-in customer, I want to see the status of every order I've placed in the last 12 months, so that I don't have to email support.

### What
1. Logged-in customers can view a list of their orders from the last 12 months
2. Each order shows current status and a delivery estimate
3. A carrier tracking link is shown when one is available

The codebase is a TypeScript Next.js app with a Postgres DB accessed via Prisma. There's an existing `orders` table and an authenticated `/account` route group. Carrier tracking data comes from a third-party API we already call elsewhere for the admin panel. Write the implementation plan.
evals.expected_output: A structured implementation plan with Approach (one sentence), a Changes table, a Breakdown citing real-ish symbols/paths, a Files table, and a Test Strategy mapped to the three ACs. Should contain no status-quo description, no rationale/why, no risks/tradeoffs, no open-questions section, and no thought-process preamble.
assertions: Plan has a '🎯 Approach' section and it is a single sentence
Plan has a '🛠️ Change Summary' section rendered as a markdown table (logical units of work with one-line summaries)
Plan has a '🧱 Breakdown' section expanding the changes with concrete detail (signatures, snippets, data shapes, or paths)
Plan has a '📂 Files Touched' section rendered as a markdown table listing files created/modified/deleted
Plan has a '🧪 Test Strategy' section that maps to the three acceptance criteria
Section headers and emoji match the template exactly (🎯 Approach, 🛠️ Change Summary, 🧱 Breakdown, 📂 Files Touched, 🧪 Test Strategy)
Breakdown references concrete paths/symbols consistent with the described stack (Next.js routes, Prisma models)
Plan contains NO open-questions or assumptions section
Plan contains NO status-quo/background re-description of the current system
Plan contains NO why/justification prose (states decisions, not the case for them)
Plan contains NO risks-considered or tradeoffs/rejected-alternatives section
Plan opens directly with the Approach — no 'here's my thinking'/'let me walk through' preamble

evals.prompt:
We've got an approved spec for adding rate limiting to our public API:

### Title
Protect public API from abuse

### Why
A handful of clients are hammering the API and degrading service for everyone.

### What
1. Requests beyond a per-client threshold are rejected with a clear error
2. Clients can see their current usage against the limit
3. Internal services are not affected by the limit

The API is a Python FastAPI service behind a load balancer; we run multiple replicas. There's a Redis instance available. Plan the implementation.
evals.expected_output: The spec is genuinely ambiguous on shape-changing decisions (what the per-client threshold is, how a 'client' is identified, whether limits are global-across-replicas or per-replica, what 'internal services' means for exemption). A good run asks these blocking questions BEFORE writing the plan, rather than producing a plan full of assumptions or an open-questions section. After answers it would produce a decisive plan.
assertions: Run surfaced blocking clarifying questions BEFORE writing the plan
Clarifying questions cover shape-changing forks: how a 'client' is identified, the threshold value/window, cross-replica vs per-replica counting, and what counts as an exempt 'internal service'
Clarifying questions are concrete and offer options, not vague
Plan has a '🎯 Approach' section and it is a single sentence
Plan has a '🛠️ Change Summary' table, a '🧱 Breakdown', a '📂 Files Touched' table, and a '🧪 Test Strategy' section
Section headers and emoji match the template exactly
Test Strategy maps to the three acceptance criteria (rejection, usage visibility, internal exemption)
The plan artefact itself contains NO open-questions or assumptions section despite the underlying ambiguity
Plan contains NO status-quo/background, NO why/justification prose, and NO risks/tradeoffs section
Plan opens directly with the Approach — no thought-process preamble
Plan commits to specific decisions (e.g. a concrete identification scheme and a cross-replica Redis counter) rather than hedging

evals.prompt:
Quick one — approved spec:

### Title
Add a /healthz endpoint

### Why
Our load balancer needs a liveness probe; right now it pings / which does real work.

### What
1. GET /healthz returns 200 with body 'ok' when the service is up
2. The endpoint does no database or downstream calls

It's a Go service using the chi router; routes are registered in `internal/server/routes.go`. Write the plan.
evals.expected_output: A very short plan proportional to a trivial change — likely a one-sentence Approach, a one- or two-row Changes table, a brief Breakdown, a small Files table, and a one-line Test Strategy. Should NOT be inflated with ceremony, and should not ask unnecessary clarifying questions (there are no shape-changing ambiguities here). No open questions, no rationale padding.
assertions: Plan has a '🎯 Approach' section and it is a single sentence
Plan has a '🛠️ Change Summary' table, a '🧱 Breakdown', a '📂 Files Touched' table, and a '🧪 Test Strategy' section
Section headers and emoji match the template exactly
Plan is short and proportional to a trivial change (roughly 30 lines or fewer of rendered markdown)
Change Summary table has only one or two rows — the work is not inflated into ceremony
Breakdown references the chi router and the real path internal/server/routes.go
Test Strategy is brief and maps to the two acceptance criteria (200 'ok'; no DB/downstream calls)
Run did NOT ask unnecessary clarifying questions — there are no shape-changing ambiguities here
Plan contains NO open-questions/assumptions section, NO status-quo, NO why/justification, NO risks/tradeoffs
Plan opens directly with the Approach — no preamble
